headline: Joyce on Littler’s 150 bull finish: ‘quite an easy one to hit’
standfirst: Ryan Joyce, a regular on the bullseye route, says the three-bull checkout is far less daunting for professionals than it looks.
body: Ryan Joyce has played down the 150 checkout that Luke Littler produced at the Grand Slam of Darts, saying the three-bullseye route is not as hard for a professional as it appears from the stands or on television.

Littler's finish came against Niels Zonneveld in Group A at Wolverhampton. Facing 150 with his opponent on the brink of victory, the defending champion hit bull, bull, bull to force a deciding leg. Zonneveld went on to win the match 5-4, although Littler still reached the last 16 as one of the group's qualifiers.

Most players treat 150 as a treble 20 or treble 19 finish, which leaves either double 15 or double 18 for the last dart. Very few go for the bull route regularly, but Joyce is one of them, and he explained why on the radio.

"I do like having a go at it," Joyce said. "I think it's quite an easy one to hit if you get the first one in because we practise it so often." He added that the challenge lies in putting the three darts together, and that once the first bullseye is in, repeating the same action twice more is not as hard as it sounds for a professional.
Joyce, who is known as 'Relentless', said that the bull is not his favourite part of the board. He is more associated with double 16, and says he fancies hitting any finish that ends on it.

Joyce's comments are a reminder that the finish, while rare on television, is a deliberate choice for some players rather than a lucky accident. Littler's version came when he needed it most, and it kept him in a match he went on to lose by a single leg.
